After just over 30 days the batteries stopped working. I rinsed them several times successfully, and they worked fine, but now they only work if they’re plugged in.

We got two of these. These have a really long battery life. Haven't timed it, but 24 hours PLUS. They do get lots of the smaller bugs. They rinse off easily too. We didn't get them for the light, but that seems to work well too.

They work much better if there's not a lot of other light around - we turn them on inside at night after we've gone to bed and by the morning it's zapped most of the little bugs in the room they're in.

They aren't as satisfying as the old-school bug zappers we had as kids that would get big ones like big flies and moths, and since they work better when it's dark (like no other lights on), we tend to not see them in action like with the old kind that put out a lot more light.

text_fidelity_a: Etekcity Camping Air Mattress Inflatable Single High Airbed Blow up Bed Tent Mattress with Rechargeable Air Pump, Height 9", Carry Bag I have been through 4 air mattresses and each one sucked, so I was not expecting much from this one. I didn't even want to try another one, but to get my partner to agree to go camping I had to supply an air mattress so I went with the one with the highest rating within my budget and waited to be disappointed. Imagine my surprise. You can charge the pump from your vehicle (no batteries! which was great because they didn't even cross my mind) or from a regular outlet. The pump is noisy but not unusually so, and the mattress inflated pretty darn quick. It was ample for 2 large people and 2 small dogs. Best of all, incredibly, it didn't deflate overnight! I did "top it off" a bit for the 3rd night but over-all it was full and comfy, survived excited dogs and 40 degree weather, the pump has a reverse so you can deflate it really fast, and somehow, someway, it actually all fit back easily into the box it came in so we can keep it safe for next time. It wasn't even overpoweringly stinky like plastic usually is (we still aired it out of course, how stinky is too stinky being quite subjective but neither of us was bothered).  If someone asked me to recommend an air mattress, I would gleefully direct them to this one.
text_fidelity_b: Etekcity Camping Air Mattress Inflatable Single High Airbed Blow up Bed Tent Mattress with Rechargeable Air Pump, Height 9", Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Perfect Life Ideas 3 Pack Camping Lanterns LED Lamps Emergency Lights for Home Vehicle Travel Emergencies - Garage Office Desk Camp Rv Boat. Battery Operated Lighting Gear. Cordless. Brand Tm These are small - roughly the same size as a coke can - and that makes them the perfect size for some very specific uses. They weigh almost nothing, even with the four AA batteries inserted. The little handle on top is just tall enough to hang these lanterns from a drawer pull or in our house, a push down style door knob. With the light weight, the lantern hangs without affecting the use of the door handle so you can have light in an interior room or basement while hunting for a fuse box etc and know where the exit is. I also like that the exterior of the lantern is a bit of a rubberized texture - setting it on our marble bathroom counter in the dark wasn't as risky as it would've been with just slick plastic. These are small and weigh very little - a slippery surface or wet hands could be a problem without the textured case.

The light is very bright and clear white. No yellow hue to it at all and these LED bulbs turn on instantly. We tested the lights in a pitch black garage, closet and walking around in the back yard at 11pm. They are bright enough to use to get dressed or find your way around the garage with no problems at all. Use in the yard was fine, but a flashlight is better as a directional aimed beam for walking. My one star deduction is because I dropped one of the lanterns from hip high and it came apart when it landed (a fall of two feet onto a thick bath mat). The batteries flew out and the bottom cracked apart. However - the light DID work afterwards and we just super glued the crack back together. I'll keep these in the bathroom, garage and kitchen for power outages in the future. I received a sample set for testing and review.
text_fidelity_b: Perfect Life Ideas 3 Pack Camping Lanterns LED Lamps Emergency Lights for Home Vehicle Travel Emergencies - Garage Office Desk Camp Rv Boat. Battery Operated Lighting Gear. Cordless. Brand Tm

text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell So far, this is a great bell! I just installed it today after I received it in the mail. It looks and fits great on my 2022 Trek Marlin 6. I was in my garage checking out the new bell and ringing it a few times while my wife was about 40 feet away outside in the driveway talking with her friend who was parked in the driveway with her car running and they both said that they could easily hear the bell. Her friend was in her car and my wife was standing outside the car, mind you, that car was not quite with the cooling fans running and the wind was also blowing to create extra noise. Yes, this bell is plenty loud to get someone's attention. This bell also allows you to rotate the dinger in any position you want, which gives you the ability to position exactly where it is best for you. You just rotate the assembly below the bell and put it how you want it. This is a very well thought out design that works great!

Another example later that evening, I was riding down a pathway that parallels the roadway and as I was approaching a parking lot driveway, there were two vehicles stopped waiting to exit to the roadway. I decided to continue down the pathway between the rear of one vehicle and the front of the other vehicle. But just to make sure that the second car saw me coming, I slowed and chimed the bell three times to get her attention as I was approaching about 25 feet away. She looked up and at me, smiled and waved as I slowly rode between the two vehicles. The bell worked as designed. The construction seems to be sturdy, but time will tell. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a small bell that does the job.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell

All the reviews make it out to be something it most certainly is not. This is just a novelty kit with about $5 work of product (if that). Neat concept, poor execution. If you're looking for a survival kit with products that will actually help you survive something in real life...THIS IS NOT IT. Even as a themed novelty kit, this is junk. Save your money.

The most useful items are the anti-bacterial goop and the bandaids.

The card multi-tool could be useful, but ALL the edges are sharp and can easily break skin.

The "tactical knife" is a card-knife that can neither be properly locked open or properly locked closed. It struggled with cutting the plastic this survival kit came wrapped in.

The dust mask is unfinished on the edges. It can easily become unraveled and had lots of loose ends fresh out of the package.

There was a tea candle. Yep.

Compass did not point North. Ever.

Glow sticks were not bright enough to illuminate the desk they were lying right on.

The fire starter is a joke. Don't get me wrong..With some skill it can be used, but it is absolute junk. I broke the metal bar after a few practice tries.

Overall, if I hadn't had a gift card to waste, I would have returned the item for a refund. Even my son who is all about zombie survival thought it was junk.

text_fidelity_a: Gifts for Men Dad, Fathers Day, Husband Grandpa -Survival Kit Gear 16 in 1-Fishing Camping Hunting Hiking Gifts Ideas for Him-Cool Gadget Survival Gear We have been working on assembling a couple go bags for our family in case of an emergency, such as a natural disaster, fire, etc. WORSPODAY's 16-in-1 survival kit is the perfect addition to it. First of all, the price is on point and provides a huge savings over having to buy each of the items included individually. Second, we love the watertight hardback case that the tools come in. It has strong clasps on three sides and they don't just pop open. You have to tug pretty hard on them, so that actually is important so you don't lose your gear when you're on the move and may need it most. Second, the tactical gear that is included isn't cheaply made. These are durable products, such as the tactical pen (with a glass breaker on one end), flashlight (needs one AA battery), and the knife. Even the compass is fairly weighty in your hand and works very well. Also, because of the amount of detail that goes into these items, this whole kit makes a handsome gift that any outdoorsman would appreciate too. We also like the tactical bracelet because even if that is all you have on you, there is also a flint built in so you can start a fire, a whistle, and a compass. Also, it is made of paracord, so you can use it to tie up an emergency shelter or go fishing if need be. The manual that comes with it is detailed, but you will want to become well familiar with each item included and how to use it before you head out to the woods or on your trek as you may try to outrun a storm. Also, there are a few items included such as the glass breaker end of the pen, the saw, and of course the knife, which could cut someone, particularly a child, so you'll want to make sure those who handle it aren't going to accidentally injure themselves because these items are definitely not toys. All in all, however, this is an exceptional product, and I plan to recommend it to everyone I know who may be putting together their own go bag.

Magpul Terrain Sunglasses Tactical Ballistic Sports Eyewear Shooting Glasses for Men I own a variety of sunglasses from Serengeti, Ray Ban, Oakley, Tag Heuer, etc... All are get marked up a lot due to brand names and Luxoittca's grip on the market, but all have excellent lenses, especially the Serengeti and Oakley lenses. I tend to pay $100-150 for these (often shopping around and waiting for deals), so seeing these for $127 raised my expectations, despite being well aware of Magpul's heritage for reliable, often ugly, and occasionally overpriced bits of plastic.

These are reliable ugly overpriced frames. Well ugly is a bit harsh, but compared to designer eyewear brands, these look more like $30 frames than $130 designs. They are especially reliable in terms of grip., I've never had glasses more glued to my head than these. They don't move at all when upside down, shaking my head, etc... Great work there. Comfort is Ok. Not great, but considering how well they stay in place, it's not bad. The optics are OK. Nothing special in terms of clarity, color rendition, or contrast. Not at all in the same league as Serengeti, Oakley, or even Tag Heuer.

I'd be much more forgiving at $80, but these are $130. The overall image is comparable to $10-15 knock off lenses from eBay. I'm sure these are decent quality in regards to UV and whatnot, but in terms of clarity and contrast, they're just so-so.

If these had lenses on par with my Tag Heuer Sennas, I'd be in love. Sure they're not the best looking frames, but the sure grip and wide field of view would make up for that. These are functional glasses, not fashion ones. Sadly the functional quality of the lenses just falls short.

text_fidelity_a:
OASMU Sand Free Beach Blanket Picnic Mat I live in an area about equidistant from the beach and the mountains. I like going to the beach but I much prefer the mountains, particularly in the autumn when the leaves change. One of the simple pleasures in life is having a picnic in the mountains, and this particular beach blanket is a good accessory for those trips.

This is not a blanket in the traditional sense. There is no padding, no fiber, no fringe. This is a very thin cover made of parachute nylon and it is very lightweight and thin. It will not provide any insulation from hard ground, nor will it provide much in the way of drying off after getting wet, but it is very water resistant and it will keep you from getting wet from wet ground unless you put it down on standing water.

Because this is such a lightweight blanket it means that it can be caught up with a good gust of wind. Provision has been made for that. There are pockets on the corners and they can be filled with sand at the beach or with stones when farther away. There are also loops on the corners for securing with pegs. Unfortunately there are no pegs included with this blanket and that is the one thing I would suggest for improvement.

I have a special use for this blanket. Along the Blue Ridge parkway there are picnic areas and my family and I like to go there for a nice picnic lunch. The blanket makes a perfect (although very large) tablecloth for the picnic table. When we’re done, it is very easy to clean and it packs up for the next trip with little effort.

I love the fact that this blanket compacts down to a size smaller than a football. It folds up very neatly and compactly and it fits in a pretty blue nylon bag with a pull tie. At that size it is small enough to fit in a shoulder bag or in just about any space in the car when traveling.

This is a very well-made blanket, too. I have found no issues with the stitching, the seams are straight and there are no nicks or cuts in the nylon material. I imagine that will change over years of use, but so far it still is pristine.

I am very happy with this beach blanket. It serves me well on picnics in the mountains, which is really all I could ask for. It is made well, it’s plenty large, and there are some thoughtful features that went into it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: OASMU Sand Free Beach Blanket Picnic Mat

I give it 2 stars due to Fortified's stellar customer service. I wrote them about the issue and they mailed me some rubber bumpers to help hold the battery inside the housing. G4Free 2/4/13 PCS Camping Cookware Mess Kit Hiking Backpacking Picnic Cooking Bowl Non Stick Pot Knife Spoon Set This is a decent set of camping cookware consisting of four pots, each with handles (but no lids). The set nestles together into a pretty compact stack that measures about 7 inches tall and about 5 inches wide. It also comes with a mesh pouch to hold the pots when they are stacked together. It makes for a small, easily toted package.

The build quality is decent but not exceptional. The pans are aluminum and somwhat thin. The metal is thick enough so that the pots won't dent easily, but you can flex the pan if you squeeze them hard. The handles have a silicon coating on them which is nice for helping with heat protection (although you still need a mitt or pad to grab the handle if the pot has been on the fire for a while). The handles fold easily and take up very little room. However, the bracket that attaches the handles to the pot, as well as the handles themselves, are not all that sturdy. They are functional, but won't stand up to much (or any) abuse.

The pot sizes are fine for cooking for one or two people (perhaps you could stretch it to three if everyone is a light eater).

For occasional camping (or the rare emergency) use, these are more than durable enough to get the job done, and do so in a very space-conservative fashion. For that, I'd give them 4-stars. If, however, you're an especially avid camper, or need to cook for more than two people, you'll probably want a larger, more durable set.

FoxFury RUGO RCS Drone/Camera/Utility, 620 Lumens, Strobing This is a great video camera light. Very sturdy metal housing is heavy, but should last a long time. It comes with a variety of interchangeable mounts so you can use it with GoPro cameras, standard tripod mounts, or cameras with standard flash mounts. There are mounting points on the top and bottom of the light so you could mount the light to a tripod, then mount a GoPro on top of it. The light has various brightness settings so you can use it at different distances or with different camera settings. I love that it has different field of view settings: wide angle floodlight for closeups, midrange area light, and long distance spotlight that is good for up to 98 feet. The light beam is even across the whole area, not like a flashlight that is much brighter in the center. The kit comes with a nice soft carrying case as well as a wall charger. The charger uses a standard micro-USB cable, so you could also use your cell phone charger.

My only complaint is that the GoPro adapters are all lightweight plastic and will eventually break if you use them a lot. The way the adapters mount to the camera is proprietary and I do not know how easy they will be to replace.

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm) I admit, I have a bit of a "thing" with trying new yoga mats. I have a mat that I love and that I use for most purposes, including practicing both at home and in class, which is my [[ASIN:B00AB3LLVS Manduka eKo Lite Yoga Mat]]. However, I also own other mats I use for other purposes, such as keeping one at work, one for Pilates, etc.

I was interested in this Gaiam mat because it is thicker than my eKo Lite, 5mm as compared to 3mm. Although I like my think Manduka, I thought than the thicker Gaiam mat might be good for occasions when I have to practice on particularly hard flooring. Upon unrolling the mat, I did like that it was thick but FIRM--i.e., it was not squishy. This mat is designed to be two-sided. The first side, which has a texture, is described as the more "traditional" side. At first, I thought that this side would provide more stability, but as soon as I stepped on it, I found that my feet were sliding around.

Given this, I decided to try the mat on the smooth side, which is the design side. This side definitely had more of a "sticky" feel. Upon first use, my feet felt secure upon the mat: the mat did feel like a "sticky mat," and my standing poses felt good. Therefore, I decided to take the mat with me to yoga class the next day, which was a free class held in a room with concrete floors. Just getting the mat there was a bit of a feat, as 1) the mat was a VERY tight fit in my [[ASIN:B000VW4VWA Manduka MatSak Yoga Bag]] (designed for full-size Manduka mats), and 2) the mat is much heavier than my eKo light. But worse, taking the mat to class was a mistake. Initially, standing poses were okay, but my hands continually slid on the mat in down dog. Furthermore, as the mat got a bit sweaty, it just got more slippery and felt quite unsafe.

This is a pretty mat and feels to be very high quality. I may continue to use it at home for Pilates and abs work, but due to stability problems, I cannot recommend it for yoga.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm)

text_fidelity_a:
SEAFLO 42-Series Water Pressure Diaphragm Pump w/Variable Flow For Reduced Cycling - 12V, 3.0GPM, 55PSI This is an interesting pump. It works really well, but there are some things to keep in mind.

First, it's a 1/2" line. In and out. Hooking it up to a 5/8" or 3/4" hose really cuts the pressure. However, put it on a 1/2" line (I used PEX) and the pressure is good.

Second, the NPT connections work really well, but you will need some adapters if you want to connect it to other things. There is a Garden hose threat adapter out there for a fair price. However, the barbed connector provided doesn't work well with PEX. There are PEX to NPT connectors easily available.

Third, you need a good, ridged intake pipe. I tried some clear poly tubing and it more or less collapsed as the intake. Of course that really cut down on the output.

So, with the correct adapters you can get it to work well for things other than campers. Just don't expect it to be "plug and play".
text_fidelity_b: SEAFLO 42-Series Water Pressure Diaphragm Pump w/Variable Flow For Reduced Cycling - 12V, 3.0GPM, 55PSI

text_fidelity_a:
JACO MBX-60 Presta Tire Pressure Gauge for Bikes (Max 60 PSI) | MTB & XC Series The old saying that a person who has one watch always knows what time it is, but a person who has two watches is never sure, comes to mind here. If this is your only pressure gauge and you dial in your tire pressures based on this tool, you’ll be happy. But if you have a couple of different gauges like me, some on pumps and another that is independent like this one, then you won’t be exactly sure which one is accurate.

However, consistency and precision is what matters. Based on several years of use and comparison to two other gauges and my car readouts, I trust my digital gauge on my bike floor pump for accuracy from psi ranges in the mid teens to the mid 50s. I took readings from several different pressures as benchmarked with my pump, and this analog gauge consistently read about 1 psi lower. That consistency is more than good enough for me. And by way of background, I’ve set up my mountain bike and gravel bike with tubeless tires, and I am particular about the pressures I run in different conditions.

Also, this gauge has a rubberized face and comes in a sturdy and well padded case. Since this is a precision instrument, I appreciate the protection to keep this device working well.

Overall this is an easy to use tool that feels like it will last a long time (as long as you don’t abuse it).
text_fidelity_b: JACO MBX-60 Presta Tire Pressure Gauge for Bikes (Max 60 PSI) | MTB & XC Series

text_fidelity_a:
Discraft 160 Gram Sky Styler Sport Disc I really like this disc for throw and catch frisbee in light to know winds. Mostly I throw a 175G Innova Pulsar. But in no wind to light breezes this think is a blast to throw. I throw frisbee with a partner a couple of days a week and I've been throwing on and off since, cough-cough, the 80's.

This disc will do more in a light wind than the 175g Ultimate discs. Meaning you can curve it, it will drift a bit on the wind, catch an updraft and float, etc. It's also great for throwing it as hard as you can since it's lighter and easier to catch. It's also a great disc for warming up before getting out a heavier disc. You wouldn't think 15G would make much of a difference but you definitly feel the difference when throwing a catching.

I don't know if it's a thing for freestyle, but it has no thumb grooves on top. After a couple of throws I stopped even noticing it didn't have them.

It's just a really good all around disc for throw and catch frisbee if you don't need the the weight of a 175g disc.all the time. If I could only have one disc, it would be the 175g Pulsar but since I can have more than one disc, this would be the 2nd disc if I could only have 2.

Also for a beginning thrower, who wants something to toss around at a picnic, with the kids in the backyard this is the better choice than the heavier 175g discs. For young kids while I haven't thrown it you might want to consider the even lighter J-Star. from Discraft.
text_fidelity_b: Discraft 160 Gram Sky Styler Sport Disc

text_fidelity_a:
Profile Designs FC 35 Hydration System - 35oz Pros: This is an excellent hydration system for TT / triathlon bikes. It stays put without rattling around, even on bumpy roads. You have to tighten the little screws to set the mount on the bars correctly or it will rattle (just follow the directions that come with it!). I experienced no sloshing of liquids out of the unit except when I overfilled it (totally my fault, lesson learned). It's easy to drink out of when in aero position. The aero design is excellent. The computer mount is exactly where I need it! I don't have to look down to see my Garmin 920xt mounted on its quick release to the F35 computer mount. It's very heads up without costing anything aerodynamically. The compartment for extras holds quite a bit. I can jam some bonk busters and gels into it and the bands keep them from flying out. Super easy to refill on the go. I have one bottle cage on the front tube. I can easily take that large bottle, turn it upside down and refill the F35 without breaking or stopping.

Cons: Not easy to take off for cleaning. The mounts are supposed to stay on the bike and you're supposed to just remove the hydration chamber. However, the TINY little velcro strap to release the chamber is in a hard to get to spot and if you have anything more than tiny hands with tiny fingers, you will struggle to grab the velcro to release and then re-attach it. Can be a BEAR to clean! Fortunately, I have what amounts to a oversized pipe cleaner that I use for my thermos and bottles so I'm able to get into the nooks and cranies to clean it. The straw is difficult to get back in if you remove it for cleaning (which ya kinda need to do!). The little o-ring where the straw goes into the unit can pop into or out of the unit when re-inserting the straw after cleaning. All of these cons are very easy to deal with if you realize it.

Major con (and the loss of one star): The cost! Sheesh! Expensive for what you get. I got mine for $77.77 here on Amazon. Shop around to get the best price.

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks… I had high hopes for these electric socks. I mean, electric blankets have been around forever, right? So maybe, just maybe these would work. Sadly, they are utter crap.

When they arrived, they didn't look too bad. I was concerned about how much of the sock would have a heated area, but I figured, even a relatively small area might be helpful. I got some fresh AA batteries and loaded up the battery compartments. (There is a little pocket near the top outer side of each sock. There is a wire inside each of these that connects to the battery box.)

I felt just the faintest bit of warmth from one sock and nothing from the other. I put them on and honestly could not tell a difference between the non-working side and the one that was faintly warm. I thought perhaps they needed more time to warm up, so I continued wearing them hoping that would happen. I was busy working and after a couple of hours realized that they had never warmed up. So I decided to check the batteries, 'just in case,' they weren't fully charged. When I checked them on my battery tester, all four were completely dead even though I had gotten them from my fresh supply. I wondered if they could possibly have been bad to begin with, though that seemed highly unlikely. Then I wondered if the box had somehow drained the batteries.

Still holding out a tiny bit of hope the socks would warm, I got out more batteries. This time I checked them with my battery tester first, to make sure they were fully charged. They were. Again I felt the tiniest bit of warmth and thought, "Great! I guess the last batch of batteries were no good."

Put them on and again, could not feel the warmth. I later checked the fully charged batteries and .. you guessed it, they were drained. So not only did the stupid socks not work, they somehow drained EIGHT AA batteries!! What a waste of time and money. Needless to say, I want to send these back.

It's really a shame because a lot of people would love to have socks like this if they would actually work. I hope the manufacturer figures out a way to make them work AND do so without having to go through dozens of batteries each week.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks…

text_fidelity_a: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag First of all, I used to be one of those people who thought trekking poles were for wusses, but as I've gotten a bit older and wiser I have found that they are indispensable for longer hikes. I can hike twice as far with them and they really help with some challenging up and downs. These poles look great and are comfortable to use.  I went on one 10 mile hike when I first used them. I did find that the pole adjustment locks took some getting used to.  You have to turn a knob and then flip the clip to lock it into position. If you tighten the screw too much then there is too much tension and you can't flip the clip, so you have to go back and loosen the screw a bit more and then try again. Once I got the hang of it, it was fairly simple. I would suggest doing it before you leave the house. I'd also suggest leaning hard on each pole to be sure it's locked firmly.  Also, when putting the mud guards on, it helps to screw them on to the threads at the pole bases and then push on firmly. I lost one mudguard (in some really deep mud.) The Foxelli company's customer service is excellent though and they sent a replacement pair out right away!  These come with a nice bag and two sets of tips (one for storage and one for asphalt) and two sets of guards (one for dirt and one for snow.)

text_fidelity_a:
Head by Mares Seaview 180° Panoramic View Full Face Snorkel Mask Natural Breathing Snorkeling, (Designed and Made in Italy) I snorkel maybe once a year, and never really love it. I tend to do most of my day-to-day breathing through my nose, and when forced to use my mouth I go into a bit of subconscious panic mode that takes a while to wear off and makes the whole snorkel experience less fun and relaxing than it should be. So when I read about full-face masks I was excited to be able to finally snorkel with no issues at all. I read up on the potential safety risks as well, and decided on this model, as one of the few on the market that appears to have been tested for CO2 issues.

Upon receiving the mask I tried it on and found it to be easy enough to deal with. I tried it on in my house and found it to be pretty comfortable and breathing to be no issue at all. Later I took it to a pool to give it a better test before going into the ocean and discovered that I had to lock down the straps quite a bit in order to get a waterproof fit. This made it less comfortable -- but not too bad all in all. Visibility, I noticed right away, was amazing, and a huge upgrade from what I'm used to with "traditional" snorkel gear.

As I swam around in the pool I started feeling a touch lightheaded and realized that I didn't see any bubbles coming up around me when I breathed out -- which struck me as odd, given that the mask is designed to release air through holes on the bottom.

After experimenting a bit I realized what was going on. Although I could breath fine and normally on land, the additional pressure exerted on the outside of the mask by being in water was causing the flaps to not open enough to release the stale air. Eventually I found a solution to this problem: Do not breath normally. Instead, take a fairly large breath, hold it for a bit, and then forcefully exhale. This produces enough counter pressure to open the flaps, releasing the stale air and allowing enough new oxygen to flow in to keep your brain happy.

Problem sorted I went on my vacation, went out on a boat, and spent some time in the water snorkeling. I was able to see lots of great stuff thanks to this mask, and I was able to swim more naturally/comfortably and keep my head down for longer than I've ever been able to before. And that's great. But I had to remember to do my "special" breathing pattern the whole time. Occasionally my focus would wander, I'd forget, and I'd feel my head getting foggy. And every time that happened, in the back of my head there would be a little voice telling me "this may not be safe. You're going to suffocate." And that sort of ruined the experience.

Plusses after that big negative: No fogging at all. Perfect visibility. No water leakage at all. That was a first for me when snorkeling -- I didn't taste salt water even once.

Maybe there's a better solution to the breathing problem. Maybe I just need more practice. Or maybe the tech is simply not there yet. Either way, I can't really recommend this product based on my experience. I really wanted to love it, and I hope that someday I can have a truly amazing snorkel trip. But for now I'm not really sure what I'll do. Part of me wants to try this again, and part of me is afraid. Possible that I did a bit too much research prior to this purchase!
text_fidelity_b: Head by Mares Seaview 180° Panoramic View Full Face Snorkel Mask Natural Breathing Snorkeling, (Designed and Made in Italy)

text_fidelity_a:
FILA Accessories Agility Kit I have had a desire to improve my agility, having done regular exercises as a kid. I wanted to start again, so got this set. Let's take a look at this set.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
CASE
First of all, this set comes in a nice carry case. It shuts with a spring loaded clamp and has a string for carrying or hanging up.

INSTRUCTIONS
There are instruction lists in this kit. First there are general instructions. Then there are instruction sheets with photos for each piece in this kit. I highly recommend putting each of these in a clear presentation sleeve to keep them clean, in one piece and easy to refer to.

This set comes with three types of props to ;help with exercising to develop agility:
AGILITY CONES
These cones essentially work for markers in setting up various exercises. Some of the activities are to run through and are done on your feet. Others are done with shuffling and bending to touch them. The cones are close to the ground and have a hole in the middle for grass to pop through if necessary.

AGILITY HURDLES
These are low to the ground and you set them up to do various running, stepping, and hopping over in various ways. These are tubular blue plastic with black plastic caps on the ends. These are not overly sturdy and if it is a windy day, they tend to migrate if not on the grass or other rougher surface. There is a web belt that you use to keep them together when not in use that has velcro on the ends.

AGILITY LADDER
This is a web ladder. There are hooks included to hold the ladder into place on the ground. There are exercises for hopping, skipping, running, and shuffling.

CAUTION
There are cautions provided with each exercise sheet to help those who might be a bit over ambitious not to over do it too fast.

HOW DID THIS WORK OUT FOR ME?
I was able to use this for a while to increase my agility. When we got a rainy season I could not do it anymore, and now it is winter, so I am waiting for spring again. On a gym floor these would not be as nice- they would easily slide out of place and I would spend more time fixing them than using them. I prefer using these on the grass or dirt.

This is a decent starter set. Once you get committed to using it, you can move up to something a bit more intense. However, this is easy to take with you and transport to keep you going when you have to leave and go on vacation or somewhere else for business, etc.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a great basic set that is best used on grass or ground, this set helps develop basic agility skills. It can also be brought on vacation or business trips to keep in shape if that is needed, as it is small enough to take with you if you have room for it.

MY RATING
FOUR stars. It is not quite as practical to use on anywhere but grass/ground, but it is decent and I like the way it packs away to take with me.
text_fidelity_b: FILA Accessories Agility Kit

Epson PULSENSE PS-100 Heart Rate Monitor with Activity Tracking for iOS - Black M/L The Pulsense seems like a pretty cool heart rate monitor in theory, but unfortunately falls a bit short in actual use. It’s easy to put on the wrist, and the M/L size fit me fine. It’s not too obtrusive, and while not sexy, it’s not horrendous looking either.

Setting up the device and syncing it with my iPhone was pretty easy. And it was comfortable enough to wear all day at first. But the lights and vibrations that notify you on your heart rate (what target zone you’re in) got annoying real fast – thankfully they can be deactivated. And I found myself reflexively looking at the unit whenever I wanted to know the time – but there’s no clock on it, doh! I really wish there was a digital readout that could toggle between clock and heart rate.

When it works, I like the Pulsense a lot. But I found a lot of lapses in data collection, specifically with the heart rate. At times, it shows that I was at a resting heart rate, when I know that I was actually very active. Not really sure why this happens, and I haven’t been able to pin point it to any specific activity, location, etc.

While there is a lot of potential with the Pulsense (especially not having to wear a chest strap), I’m not so sure that it’s ready for prime time. I’m excited to see how the next version will be improved.

Keystand Kids Snorkel Mask Full Face, Breathing Mechanism Snorkeling Masks, Flat Crystal Lens, 180° Panoramic Anti-Leak/Anti-Fog Mask and Snorkel with Detachable Camera Mount I've used a mask and snorkel for fun, for at least the last 50 years, and spent over 20 years as a professional scuba diver, as part of my job. I've always used a traditional mask for snorkeling and diving, and have had my share of leaky seals, fogged glass, broken hardware, and mouthfuls of salty water. This new generation of full-face masks with an integrated snorkel really does represent a breakthrough, in several respects.

I was intrigued when I first saw integrated full-face snorkel masks like this one a few years ago, and have finally decided to give one a try. I'm glad that I did.

There are many design features that really do make this snorkel mask a game changer for me. I particularly like the separate, sealed compartments that separate your eyes/cheeks/forehead from your nose and mouth. This minimizes fogging that can be caused by inadvertently breathing into a traditional mask through your nose, making it hard to see in the water. It also keeps any water that leaks in around your chin away from the glass that you see through. That's important to me, because I have a beard that does sometimes let water leak into my mask.

The seal on this mask is a soft, doubled-over flap that does an admirable job. I have a thin face and it is often difficult to find a mask that seals well. This one does. And it does a surprisingly good job sealing over my beard, which I try to keep short.

The air comes in through the top of the mask, and travels through one-way valves to the lower chamber where your mouth and nose are. Exhalations exit through purge valves near your jaw. This system works well, but I wish that the air opening at the top of the mask, where the snorkel enters, was larger. It sometimes feels like I have to work too hard to get a big breath of air, which can lead to a feeling of claustrophobia and, for some users, I expect, panic. A bigger airway would probably alleviate this.

There is a place to install a go-pro style action camera, which I will be using for sure. It's a thoughtful addition that will simplify saving and sharing my adventures.

The snorkel has a float valve that keeps water from flooding the mask when you dive. This sort of valve is great for playing near the surface, but probably not reliable for deep diving.

You can't use this mask for scuba diving, because there's no way to get your regulator into your mouth. For regular snorkeling though, I have a new favorite mask!
text_fidelity_b: Keystand Kids Snorkel Mask Full Face, Breathing Mechanism Snorkeling Masks, Flat Crystal Lens, 180° Panoramic Anti-Leak/Anti-Fog Mask and Snorkel with Detachable Camera Mount

text_fidelity_a:
Cat Caterpillar Camo Hydration Reservoir -2L We don't hike per se, but we do head out to the ranch in the deep West Texas borderlands a couple of times a year and you absolutely need water on your person out there. The Chihuahua desert and Chinati mountains combined with extreme temperatures out there can cause a serious hydration problem very quickly. Typically, I put two one gallon containers per person in our saddle bags and we ride out. I like the idea of having this water pouch for walking with it's built in straw.

The pouch itself is easy to see with clear sections in the camo print so you know exactly how much water you have left. The straw has a pull off cover and it pops back into place with a firm click so you know it's really closed. The fill opening is wide enough to refill with a water hose or just using the regular old kitchen faucet. I was surprised that the pouch has absolutely no plastic or chemical scent whatsoever.

My problem is the lack of velcro or any sort of straps to attach it to a backpack or belt. Basically, you have to carry it or already have a backpack with existing straps or a pocket available to hold a water pouch. It this had an attached loop even on the top, I could clip it my saddle or my jacket - I rarely use a backpack when on horseback so we'll have to retrofit something to this.

Stansport Water-Resistant Emergency First Aid Kit I selected this first aid kit to carry with me while backpacking. My thinking is that it is small and light and will have the basics down. I also knew that a full first aid kit would be better, but the asking price is low enough that it makes sense for many situations. The kit itself is fine, but like other reviews have stated the case in which the kit is stored is terrible.

I won’t rehash the contents of the kit - that’s in the product description.

The case is a side-latch case about the size of a deck of cards. The whole problem is the hinge. Mine came out of the package cracked and I can see a gap in the plastic where it should be closed around the pin, and it is a matter of time before it snaps completely and won’t close at all. My solution was to move everything to a small Lock-n-Lock which is actually waterproof and can take a lot more abuse. I will try to fix the original case with a glue gun and hope that it holds up better.

I cannot recommend this kit, even at the low asking price. The whole point of this kit is a small, compact and water resistant kit that can go anywhere. Instead, this is a kit with a fragile container that you’ll need to replace, and in that case it makes more sense to get a different kit anyway.

text_fidelity_a:
Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series) On this DVD, master instructor Cathe Friedrich offers two workouts from her Body Blast series: Supersets, a strength workout in which exercises are performed in rounds, and Push Pull, a strength workout focused on opposing muscle groups. Both workouts are very good, but what really makes this DVD so valuable is the wide variety of customization options as described below.

Supersets is a 53 minute workout. In each round, Cathe does separate exercises to work the legs, back, chest, shoulders/biceps/triceps, and core. After a brief (4-minute) warm-up, there are a total of two rounds, each broken down into two series (A and B). Cathe encourages participants to lift as heavy as possible, and she incorporates use of a barbell, dumbbells, a stability ball, and unweighted exercises as well. Many exercises are non-traditional in nature, as they include "low end" pluses as well as plyometric moves such as jump squats. The workout makes nice use of the stability ball, particularly for the core work, and Cathe finishes with 5.5 minutes of floor stretches.

Push Pull is a 45-minute, full-body weight training routine which works opposing muscle groups. In some cases, the muscle group is worked with only one exercise, whereas other muscles are targeted with several different exercises. Equipment used for this workout includes a tall step, a stability ball, a barbell, and several sets of dumbbells. The workout begins with a 3-minute warm-up which consists of some light cardio plus stretches using the tall step. Cathe then jumps right in on the legs, performing squats with the barbell, deadlifts, lunges (placing one heel on a smaller barbell to increase the work to the quads), and tall box presses. Moving on to the upper body, Cathe does chest press and rows, then ball work, includnig chest flyes and a "Y" move. Additional upper body work includes a shoulder press off the step, a one-arm row, a front raise while seated on the ball, a rear delt raise lying on the ball, bicep work with one leg on the ball for balance, and tricep dips/kickbacks. Cathe also incorporates the ball for floor leg work such as outer thigh lifts and inner thigh squeezes. There is also additional back work, abs work, and calf raises. Cathe concludes with a short (4.5 minutes) stretch that includes some nice shoulder stretches.

As mentioned above, the best thing about this DVD is the wide variety of custom options. The menus for both Supersets and Push Pull include options for playing the entire workout, viewing the chapter selections, and mixing and matching chapters. In addition, each workout offers "Quick Select Premixes" which provide both shorter and longer workout options. For Supersets, there are 14 premixes ranging in length from 28-109 minutes (these include extra cycles, upper/lower body only, etc.), and for Push Pull, there are 7 premixes ranging from 18-77 minutes which also included upper/lower body only options. Finally, there is a "Workout Blender" option which allows you to create your own custom workout by selecting chapters from either Supersets or Push Pull.

If you are familiar with Cathe, you know that she often incorporates upbeat, recognizable music (selections here include "Goldeneye," "Unbreak My Heart," "Walking in Memphis," and "Breakfast at Tiffany's"). Both workouts are solid, intermediate-level routines which will definitely help you to target virtually every body part from head-to-toe; my overall rating is 4 1/2 starts, and I would definitely recommend this DVD to others.
text_fidelity_b: Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series)

text_fidelity_a:
Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow Canvas Tent Deluxe LOVE LOVE LOVE this tent!!!
We have previously owned the classic cheaper coleman tents and when ours wore out, we bought a new coleman... upon opening it, it had tears in the seams...I boxed it up and sent it back. We were so upset by the lack of craftsmanship we decided to research better quality canvas tents. We are a young family and liked the idea of a tent that we could use for years to come. We decided on the 10x14, it's very spacious and we are able to set up a queen, and twin air mattress with plenty of room to store our bags/totes and a large dog/bed. I am a petite lady and I was able to put this tent up by myself (only took 25 min from box to erect, while stopping to look at the directions) it is a very heavy tent, but I was able to put it up with a bit of effort.
Once up I was able to really get a look at this tent... WOW! This tent is large and heavy duty! The floor is a thick rubber-like material that you can tell isn't gonna leak (and it didn't, even when there were puddles of rain water between the tarp below and tent) I sprayed the tent down (as per directions) prior to our first camping trip. And off we went...
This tent has turned heads every time we camp, it is a heavy duty, quality tent that we know will last for years to come... It is so simple to put up, and we are so pleased with our investment.
We have not yet had it stand the test of a storm, but I have no doubt it will hold up well.
As far as staying warm, the larger tent makes it difficult to stay warm, so bundle up and use warm blankets ;)

Oh, did I mention the tent storage bag?!?! It's awesome, and your tent will always fit, no need for super tight refilling to make it fit in the bag, this bag adjusts and will always fit your rolled up tent (we fold in half, then half again, roll and adjust the bag to fit )

To summarize:
Pros:
Large roomy tent that you can stand and walk around in, the walls are straight so you don't lose storage room
Durable canvas that is waterproof
Quality thick floor that will not leak
Heavy duty metal rods/poles and steaks
Large doors and windows makes the tent feel even more open and allows a cross breeze
The ingenious tent bag that will always be able to fit the tent once rolled up

Cons:
The long poles (when storing) and the weight of the tent
No electrical slot for extension cords (have to put them through the door)

Overall If you are in the market for a quality tent that will last for years to come...buy this tent!
text_fidelity_b: Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow Canvas Tent Deluxe

text_fidelity_a:
Putt-A-Bout Par Three Golf Putting Green I started out looking at several hundred dollar mats and ended up seeing this one with really good reviews for a little over 30 bucks. I was very skeptical, but decided to take a chance at that price as the length fit my area nicely, plus if I grew tired of it I was not out much money. I was really surprised that the mat was better than what I expected. It is not thick but does have a backing, rolls good and looks nice with the curved sections when placed on the floor. The section with the holes and hazards is slightly elevated with foam backing. Some cuts to the mat shape are not perfect but nothing major and hardly noticeable. All sections of the mat were flat minutes after putting on the floor. No rolled edges or corners.
We have it in a sunroom on a tile floor, rolls great and looks much better than those mats that are square and straight. However, the holes & hazard cutouts do not have a bottom (you’ll just see the floor through the holes and hazards). To keep the balls from hitting our tile floor and to make it look better, I cut out and placed a thick white poster-board under that section. My young son decided to use markers on the poster board to make one hazard blue for water and the other beige for sand. Looks pretty good!
Since the holes are not very deep, you’ll need to use finesse to not run the putt past the hole which might be the only negative. But we remedied that with a couple LEORX Indoor Golf Practice Putting Cups placed over two holes which those also have a small flag which makes the course look good. For the center hole we are using an electric ball return we already had.
Maybe the only negative is you don't have room to practice putting speed and seeing how far past the hole you went.
My home course is Bent Grass greens and while this doesn’t emulate that environment exactly, I have found these do roll true and fast which allows a person to work on putting skills, or just have fun competitions with family. My wife actually commented that she liked the fact I could roll it up when we need the floor space for company and for that price it is not big deal if we end up not using it later down the road.
I recommend this mat.
text_fidelity_b: Putt-A-Bout Par Three Golf Putting Green

text_fidelity_a:
Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black These are a good product for the price. I purchased them to give myself a little more upright position on an old mountain bike. They do this pretty well.

The reason they do not get 5 stars is the top portion where you put your hand was about 3/4 of an inch too short to mount my original twist shifters and still have room for my grips, making the place where you put your hands a little shorter than intended. OK for me, and also wouldn't be an issue for maybe a different type shifter - like the trigger type, or no shifter at all like a single speed bike. However for someone with very large hands it might be a problem.

Beyond that they appear to be pretty decent quality for the price.

Don't underestimate the amount of change in position that you will get. I paired these with a adjustable quill stem, and I think one or the other would be sufficient, so if your changing out an old mountain bike I might start with one or the other, not both. Also, due to the longer reach you will very likely need to change your shifter and brake cables. My originals were cut too short for this handlebar. Its not a difficult job, but a fair bit of work. You probably will want to buy new grips also in case your originals like mine were hard to remove.
text_fidelity_b: Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black

text_fidelity_a:
Cascade Mountain Tech Trekking Poles - Carbon Fiber Walking or Hiking Sticks with Quick Adjustable Locks Took a pair of these on the AT in 2016. They weighed 14.2 ounces* (without the baskets, or rubber tips) which is about as light as you'll find, at any price. The grips were comfortable, the straps didn't chafe, even when wet. (for medium/large man hands) One of the straps loosened initially, but once they got a bit of grit and dirt on them, it held much better. They lasted 590 miles. The metal tips were nearly worn down by that point, and the material supporting the tip blew out. Cascade doesn't sell replacement tips, but you can buy the lower third directly from Cascade at a reasonable price. The locking adjustment was rock solid, with no slippage, and they supported my 215 to 190 pound weight easily.

My far more expensive Lekkis weigh 16.3 oz. and the straps cut into my wrists.

*Edit: Bought a second pair and they weigh 15.7 oz.
text_fidelity_b: Cascade Mountain Tech Trekking Poles - Carbon Fiber Walking or Hiking Sticks with Quick Adjustable Locks

text_fidelity_a:
Sidekick Flare Vibrating Foam Roller | Lots of Features | Back Massager for Back Pain | Vibration, Heat, Bluetooth-Enabled and Interchangeable Textures for Advanced Muscle Massage. I’ve been using foam rollers with some success, so I was eager to try this vibrating roller. I found it to be easy to use, for the most part, and effective.

To simply use the roller, just press the button to turn it on. It’s simple to switch between vibration levels and to select heat or no heat. I’ve found I prefer the lowest vibration level, but I’m pretty sensitive to vibrations and things that shake me around (I get dizzy in a rocking chair!) so the higher levels were too much; I started to get a headache. I like the heat, though it doesn’t get very warm.

Two sleeves are provided: a teal one that has only slightly raised bumps on it, and a green one with much larger bumps. Again, I prefer the teal, the “easier” one. The larger bumps, especially combined with vibration, is a bit much. It’s okay on my calves, but on my back or neck, no way. I need the more gentle one.

Included is the option to download an app to guide you through some routines and to provide some suggestions on how best to use the roller to target certain areas. Downloading and pairing was easy, but I found I lost connection while in the middle of a 4-1/2 minute routine. I don't know that I’ll use the app much, maybe just refer to it if I need to focus on a certain area and am unsure of how best to accomplish that.

One more thing…the vibration when I used this on the living room floor was enough to cause some rattling of things that were sitting on the table, and enough to scare my dog. Then again, she’s afraid of most things.

Overall, this is quite a nice roller and if you’re serious about exercise and recovery, would be a good addition to your exercise equipment.
text_fidelity_b: Sidekick Flare Vibrating Foam Roller | Lots of Features | Back Massager for Back Pain | Vibration, Heat, Bluetooth-Enabled and Interchangeable Textures for Advanced Muscle Massage.

text_fidelity_a:
30MP 4K WiFi Hunting Game Trail Camera with 120°Wide Angle Monitor, Less Than 0.2s Trigger Time,Night Vision Motion Activated Waterproof Cameras, Send Pictures and Videos to Cell Phone Via Bluetooth You can get good-quality trail cameras for a lot less than this one, albeit not 4K or with as many features, but I wanted to try this one with bluetooth/wifi capability and the ability to view remotely from your phone via an app. I was also hoping to be able to download the images from the camera to my phone without having to fiddle with the memory card.

I plan to use this camera with a solar panel to keep it charged up. What I discovered is that a charged solar panel hooked to this camera will power it on, but I couldn't get the setup menu to work properly. Thinking it was probably because the camera requires batteries even if the power is not coming from the batteries, I ordered 8 AA batteries and installed them today.

After another few hours of frustration, I've decided the wifi feature of this camera is just not going to work. I have followed the instructions to a T, but I've only been able to connect to the trail camera's wifi network once, and then I could not get the Android app to allow me to look at the camera's visuals or images. Other than the 4K definition, this camera really doesn't do much more than the one I already had that cost a LOT less. It did come with a 32GB memory card, which is really nice, but I'll still have to take the card out of the camera to dump its contents onto my computer, which is a pain. I didn't want to have to unmount and take down the camera at all but to dump its contents to my phone, wipe the memory card, and be done with it.

Speaking of the app, I'm not even sure the app I finally installed (WiFiTrailCamera) is what I need to work with this camera. The instructions do not include the name of the app but only state to scan a QCode; I only found what I think might be the required app by searching online for clues. Scanning the QCode offered me some kind of smart app that required setting up an account (which made me very nervous!) and also seemed to have something to do with enterprise teams. It had nothing whatsoever to do with a trail camera. I didn't know that until I reluctantly signed up for an account so I could set up the app and review the trail camera, and then I had to uninstall it and cancel my account. QCode fail!

So right now, I'm giving this a rather positive three stars because the wifi doesn't work and the app doesn't work. I have yet to actually see any images or videos it has taken, because I just got it installed outside after a week's worth of waiting for batteries and hours of trying to get it set up, but assuming they turn out to be as high quality as advertised, I'll leave this at three stars. If the image quality is as much of a disappointment as the wifi and app were, I'll come back and take off another star.

UPDATE: Complete fail. I cannot get the camera to come on in Test mode or in On mode. It was working when I left it on its mount last night, but this morning the camera is dead and apparently did not record anything during the night. I've checked all connections repeatedly and gone through the procedures countless times. What a ripoff! I'm going back to my cheapie trail camera, which I can count on to do the job.
text_fidelity_b: 30MP 4K WiFi Hunting Game Trail Camera with 120°Wide Angle Monitor, Less Than 0.2s Trigger Time,Night Vision Motion Activated Waterproof Cameras, Send Pictures and Videos to Cell Phone Via Bluetooth

For the first hole I applied a thin layer of glue to the entire patch and stuck it over the hole in my cover.  For the second hole I applied the glue to the cover and applied the patch over the hole and glue.  The later method seemed a lot messier w/a lot of glue outside of the patch, as it's hard to apply it exactly in the same place the patch will stick.  In the end, the patch stuck to the boat cover just the same.  So, I would recommend spreading a thin layer on the entire patch and then stick the patch over the hole in the cover.  The glue dries pretty quick, but no so quick you cannot work w/it.  As of now, my patches seem to have adhered to the cover pretty well. text_fidelity_a:
Bicycle cargo trailer More evidence that there's no free lunch. I really wanted a Burley Nomad I saw on Craigslist for $100, but I was too slow and missed it. I should have either waited to find another used Burley or just paid the steep price for a new one. I wanted those three things you can't have all at the same time: fast, good, and cheap.

The Allen Explorer trailer is okay, and I do use it every week for groceries for me and the wife. For that purpose it gets me by with no problems. If that's all I wanted to do with a bike trailer it would be fine.

However, I have just started cycling to gigs (I'm a musician) and when I need to bring my own amp it's really awkward. When I think about covering real miles with a trailer my gut feeling is that this one is heavy, slow, and prone to wearing out faster than one made with an aesthetic/ethic/IDK similar to the bicycle itself - you know, ultralight, rigid, smooth rolling, made to last for decades or more.

Lately every time I have to drive my car I curse this trailer and start thinking about biting the bullet and paying for a Burley.

Besides the weight and general clunkiness of the trailer, a couple things stand out as reservations regarding a recommendation on the Allen Explorer. First, the tires are pretty weak, as others have pointed out. 30 PSI is no joke - I had a blowout after I forgot and pumped them up to 50, which is what is embossed on the tire itself; but I was able to ride home with no inner tube - even with a load of groceries - so mark a point for the cheap tires. The other thing that bugs me is that the floor of the trailer is nowhere close to rigid. It hasn't caused any problems yet, but it makes feel less enthusiastic about this trailer, and pretty much rules it out as a long-distance candidate.

For anyone thinking about getting this trailer, I would just advise you to think long and hard about what you might possibly want to do with it. Don't be like me; I've had this thing less than a year and I'm already thinking about putting down another $340 for a trailer that is very similar but very much better. I'll be lucky to get a third of my money back out of the Allen trailer.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle cargo trailer

text_fidelity_a:
cycmoto Anne Kids Bike for Toddlers and Kids, 14 16 Inch Girls Bike for 3-7 Years Old with Training Wheels and Basket, Pink, Yellow The bike arrived in good shape. Nothing was dented up and it was a reasonably smooth assembly. The tires arrived with enough air to get a few test rides in, but I wouldn't assume this to always be true and you will need to add air to the tires.

The listing states a novice can assemble this bike in 15 minutes. Unless you assemble bikes for a living it will take you longer than 15 minutes. However, this is the second bike I've assembled lately and the cycmoto was definitely easier. It will take you about 10 minutes just to unbox and remove all the foam and plastic ties. Then you will want to spend at least 10 minutes skimming through the instructions to brief yourself on the tasks at hand. I spent about 20 minutes getting all the necessary pieces together and partially tightened. Then I spent another 30 minutes adjusting, straightening, leveling and right sizing the seat, handlebars and brakes. You will want to refer to the instructions when adjusting the front brake. I did not install the training wheels, the basket or the splash guards (see comments below). So, if you just plan to assemble just the main pieces you should expect to spend about 75 minutes. If you plan to install all the extras then you should add another 30 minutes.

It comes with a flat metal multi tool and a dual size Allen wrench that can be used to completely assemble. I used the included tools to assemble. It was a little difficult for certain bolts, but it can be done. The only additional tool I used that was not included was a simple Phillips head screwdriver.

You should note that this bike has front and back hand brakes and not a coaster brake (if you pedal backwards it will spin backwards freely and not brake). The front brake (right handlebar) has two pads that squeeze the wheel to stop. The back brake (left handlebar) has a different stopping mechanism that is build into the crank system. The one concern I have with the brakes is that they are plastic. I hope they don't crack or break if the bike falls. Learning to use the hand brakes early could be better if you think the kid will grow into a mountain or bmx style bike.

A few things to note:

1) the instructions did not include a section for installing the splash guards. I am fairly confident I know which guard goes in the front/back by looking at the pictures in the listing. It would have been nice to have this in the instructions.

2) there are instructions for installing the basket, but I am either missing parts (the plate, small metal sheets and screws) or the instructions should be updated to describe attaching the basket using a ziptie like piece that was included. Personally, I would like to attach the basket as described in the instructions, but those parts were not included.

I did not install either the basket or splash guards. These are advanced attachments that should be used for kids who already know how to ride a bike with two wheels or if you plan to use training wheels. If you are purchasing this bike to train someone how to ride without training wheels then you should assume there will be a fall or two. By waiting to attach the splash guards and the basket you will avoid damaging while practicing to learn to ride a bike.

I would recommend not using the training wheels at all because it could make training without them more difficult. However, uou can adjust the height of the training wheels. So, if you start with the training wheels completely on the grown then you can slowly raise them off the ground.

Overall, the bike looks nice and feels solid.

This bike is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.

These boxing gloves came in a bright pink with neon green accents, and though I had intended to share them with my male other half, that was immediately scrapped as he was unwilling to wear such an unmanly color to work out. Good thing too, because when he tried them on, his fingers were pushing against the tips and they clearly did not fit his average sized men’s hands. If you are a man, even a smaller man, I'd recommend sizing up at LEAST to M/L but probably even larger.

As a woman, I liked these boxing gloves quite a bit. They fit my hands in an ideal fashion, gave just enough padding in just the right places that I could punch a person holding a padded shield and also use a punching bag with a reasonable amount of feedback yet absolutely no soreness or pain. Though they are brightly colored, in a workout setting that is appropriate. These are a heck of a lot nicer to use than those gross ones at the gym that everybody is allowed to use.

The one thing I didn’t like is that near the tip of the fingers, the fabric is gathered in a way that on one of my hands, feels uncomfortable. There is a thick gather of fabric right where my middle finger sets, and I found myself fidgeting with the gloves trying to unsuccessfully flatten out that bit of fabric.

Overall, these are not the most high-end gloves I’ve ever seen, but after having tried on a number of pairs, these were great in that they fit my slim hands that have long fingers very well with no pinching or discomfort, nor did they slide around during use. They seem well-made enough that I would anticipate them lasting for some time, although I do assume that anything I purchase with the express purpose of bashing it on other things may not last more than a couple years.

text_fidelity_a:
Ryno Tuff 12 Pc Resistance Bands Set - 5 Workout Bands, Cushioned Ankle Straps, Padded Handles, Door Anchor & Waterproof Gym Bag - Home Exercise, Strength Training, Physical Therapy, Yoga Fitness Gear I wanted a new set of resistance bands as my old set was getting pretty old. These Ryno-Tuff Resistance Bands Set are inexpensive and offer a good selection of bands, and - as most sets do - they come with a pair of handles, a pair of ankle straps and a door anchor. The set also includes a bag and a sturdy wall poster of exercises which those new to resistance band training could find very useful.

Let me get one thing out of the way first. The bag is small, and while you could carefully fold up all the bands and stuff the bag to make them fit, I'm not going to use the bag as putting everything into it is a pain. I'll use another bag I have that's more than twice the size so I can get to everything quickly during workouts.

Now the bands themselves. First off, they work, offering a decent amount of resistance per band. I find the material thinner than with brands like Bodylastics, which I used for years and will probably use again. If you pinch one of the thinner Ryno tubes and then one of the Bodylastics tubes, you'll notice the walls of the Ryno tubes are thinner, and don't have the snap-proof cord inside each band. That being said, Bodylastics sets cost more. These Ryno bands will get the job done, although I'm guessing that they won't last as long.

The handles are nicely padded, a plus, although the fabric used for the parts you don't grip is on the thin side, and if I were planning to go heavy with this site, I'd buy stronger handles. The ankle straps are about the same quality you get with some other resistance band sets. If you don't work heavy, they should be fine. I tore the last, very similar set I had working out at about 75 pounds, and bought something studier. I suggest you try these and see how they do for you.

But here's the thing. I have a functional trainer and weights in the house. I prefer resistance bands for certain exercises, and if you want to work out at the beach, in the park or in a hotel room, this is where resistance bands shine. If you travel a lot and prefer to work out in your hotel room, a set of resistance bands takes up little space, doesn't weigh much and are easy to use. Want to catch some rays while you work out or just want to enjoy the outdoors? Resistance bands. And if you don't have room, they're also one of the better, lower cost options.

I'll be honest - these aren't the best quality resistance bands I've used, but they're also far from the worst, and they're inexpensive, which is a plus. They allow you to stack your resistance, the handles are comfy, and the door anchor is pretty good, too. I wouldn't expect these to last as long as more premium bands, but if you don't overstretch them, they should last a while. I'm happy I got them, and I'll be using them for a while. If you're just getting into shape, the poster will be helpful, and if you travel, this set could help you work out anywhere.
text_fidelity_b: Ryno Tuff 12 Pc Resistance Bands Set - 5 Workout Bands, Cushioned Ankle Straps, Padded Handles, Door Anchor & Waterproof Gym Bag - Home Exercise, Strength Training, Physical Therapy, Yoga Fitness Gear

Explorer K2 Kayak, 2-Person Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Manual and Electric Pumps… For under 100 bucks shipped you get everything you need to get out on the water minus life vests. The skeg has been improved as it now has a new locking mechanism and silhouette. The 86" paddles are well made for the price, nicely curved, have an adjustable paddle angle and float (as we found out accidentally) so paddle leashes are recommend. The boat is stable when inflated properly using the pressure gauge "measuring strip" and did not rock too bad when standing up in the aft position with an adult seated up front. The boat has a drain plug in the stern which has to be closed as mine was shipped in the open position. The 30 gauge PVC (Vinyl) has a nylon like backing and appears to be rugged enough for large lakes and mild moving waters. Not sure I would personally use this on class III+ water but some reviewer's have reported their own success stories. It tracks well on flat water with the skeg and okay with a peaceful river current without. Seats are more comfortable than I originally imagined when purchasing. Watch out for over inflation as we pumped her up at 64° and by the afternoon the temp had increased to 74° which caused the inflation gauge to read 5-10% (0.5-1 cm) higher due to air expansion. Over all I am impressed for the cost of purchase. It comes with one 3"x3" self adhesive patch similar to "Tear-Aid type B" (looks like a square piece of yellow card stock) and two 2" clear patches that require you to use your own PVC cement. The pump tube can be stored inside the pump itself by unscrewing the end and coiling it around the pump shaft. It packs up into a Blackhawk tactical bag that I have as the Intex bag was uncomfortable to carry since it didn't have a shoulder strap. The boat is 22.2 lbs without the seats, 25.8 lbs with both seats not including other accessories.
